title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.

title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma: standardized technique and short-term outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To achieve the dual goals of effective tumor control and maximal renal function preservation, we have proposed a standardized robot-assisted nephron-sparing surgery combined with venous thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma (AML) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT). This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy. The radical-nephrectomy cohort served as a historical clinical comparator. The modified thrombectomy strategy followed the proposed "NSS" technical principles. Functional and oncological outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed without open conversion or intraoperative tumor-thrombus dislodgement, and no RAPN case required conversion to radical nephrectomy. The RAPN group had shorter operative time (160.0 vs. 232.5 min, p=0.021), shorter left renal vein clamping (3.0 vs. 16.5 min, p<0.001) and IVC clamping time (3.0 vs. 16.0 min, p<0.001), and better renal function preservation (p<0.001). Renal function was better preserved in RAPN group, primarily reflecting retention of the affected kidney. During the available follow-up (median 9 months in the RAPN group and 55 months in the Control group), no recurrence was detected; however, follow-up was insufficient for comparative or long-term oncological conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAPN with venous tumor thrombectomy appears technically feasible in patients with classic renal AML with VTT. This surgical approach could better preserve renal function, but the long-term outcomes require confirmation in larger series with longer follow-up.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy.

title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up. METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Integrated Clinical, Laboratory, and Ultrasound Model for 30-Day Venous Thromboembolic Deterioration After Acute Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BackgroundShort-term prognostic tools for venous thromboembolic (VTE) deterioration after acute lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days. Three nested ridge-penalized logistic models included clinical predictors (Model 1), clinical plus laboratory predictors (Model 2), and clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound predictors (Model 3). Missing data were multiply imputed, and the complete modeling procedure was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, incremental performance, and decision-curve net benefit were assessed.ResultsThe primary outcome occurred in 102 patients (13.0%): 82 had DVT progression and 27 symptomatic PE, with seven having both. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.702, 0.766, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.769-0.847) for Models 1-3, respectively. For Model 3, the optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.94 and Brier score 0.087. Optimism-corrected ΔAUCs were 0.064 and 0.042, with corresponding ΔBrier scores of -0.009 and -0.008. Model 3 showed the highest optimism-corrected net benefit across thresholds of approximately 8%-25%. Observed outcome proportions across risk tertiles were 3.1%, 9.6%, and 26.3%.ConclusionsModel 3 provided internally validated prediction of clinically detected VTE deterioration under local treatment and imaging practices. External validation and prospective clinical-impact assessment are required before routine use.

We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. title: A Two-Step Risk Stratification Model for Venous Thromboembolism Combining Caprini Score and D-Dimer in Trauma Patients Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adding D-dimer to Caprini score-based risk assessment can further refine venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk stratification in trauma patients, particularly among those already classified as high-risk.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 206 trauma surgical patients who underwent surgical intervention was analyzed. Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort. This threshold was not externally validated. All patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis, while patients with Caprini scores ≥9 received prophylactic-dose low-molecular-weight heparin. Bilateral lower-extremity Doppler ultrasound was performed within 24 hours of admission, with subsequent surveillance according to predefined risk criteria.ResultsOverall composite VTE incidence was 31.1%. The Caprini score showed an AUC of 0.640 for VTE discrimination. D-dimer showed the highest discrimination in the full cohort (AUC = 0.669), which decreased to 0.614 within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (≥9 points, n = 118). Applying a study-derived exploratory D-dimer threshold of ≥5.5 mg/L identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence (44.8% vs. 16.1%; RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.21-6.37, P = 0.005). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and ISS, the association was attenuated and did not remain statistically significant (adjusted OR = 2.418, 95% CI: 0.660-8.864, P = 0.183).ConclusionsRelying solely on clinical risk scoring provides limited VTE discrimination in trauma patients. A sequential two-step strategy identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence within the Caprini high-risk category, although an independent association between the D-dimer threshold and VTE was not demonstrated after adjustment. This approach warrants prospective validation in larger cohorts.

Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort.

title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

title: Association between low-dose glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement in patients with spinal dural arteriovenous fistula: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-dose glucocorticoid treatment before the diagnosis of spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF) has been associated with acute neurological worsening, but the association of a single, comparatively low dose administered during anesthesia induction with long-term neurological recovery remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021. Neurological improvement was defined as a decrease of at least 1 point in the modified Aminoff-Logue Scale score from pretreatment to the last follow-up. Patients were matched 1:1 without replacement and exactly by treatment modality using propensity scores based on age, sex, disease duration, and pretreatment neurological function. Between-group differences were evaluated using the paired risk difference, exact McNemar test, and modified Poisson regression. Glucocorticoid type and equivalent dexamethasone dose (EDD) were also evaluated among glucocorticoid-treated patients.

RESULTS: The cohort included 428 patients, of whom 172 received glucocorticoids and 256 did not. Propensity-score matching retained 167 pairs. Neurological improvement occurred in 118 of 167 patients (70.7%) in the glucocorticoid group and 119 of 167 patients (71.3%) in the nonglucocorticoid group. The paired risk difference was - 0.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], - 10.4 to 9.2; exact McNemar P = 1.000). Glucocorticoid administration was not associated with neurological improvement in the adjusted modified Poisson model (risk ratio [RR], 0.996; 95% CI, 0.871-1.138; P = 0.947), and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings. Among matched glucocorticoid-treated patients, neither glucocorticoid type (dexamethasone vs. methylprednisolone: adjusted RR, 0.979; 95% CI, 0.666-1.441; P = 0.916) nor EDD (per 5-mg increase: adjusted RR, 1.022; 95% CI, 0.931-1.121; P = 0.646) was associated with neurological improvement.

CONCLUSION: A single, comparatively low glucocorticoid dose administered during anesthesia induction was not associated with neurological improvement at the last follow-up after definitive treatment of SDAVF. No clear associations were identified for glucocorticoid type or EDD.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: High-dose glucocorticoid treatment before the diagnosis of spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF) has been associated with acute neurological worsening, but the association of a single, comparatively low dose administered during anesthesia induction with long-term neurological recovery remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021.

title: Cation-Size-Controlled Structural and Magnetic Ground State Transitions in Co2+-Based Honeycomb-Derived Oxides Na0.5RE0.5Co2TeO6 (RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y).
abstract: Honeycomb lattices containing spin-orbit-entangled Co2+ ions with effective Jeff = 1/2 moments provide promising platforms for enhancing strong quantum fluctuations and thus realizing potential quantum spin-liquid states. Here, we report a series of honeycomb-derived tellurates, "Na0.5RE0.5Co2TeO6" (NRECTO, RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y). The increased size mismatch between Na+ and RE3+ drives an orthorhombic-to-hexagonal structural transition for NRECTO, accompanied by reconstruction in the connectivity of the [Co2TeO6]2- double-rutile chains and transformation in hexagonal channel topologies. High-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction and neutron powder diffraction reveal that both structures retain similar three-dimensional Co2+ topologies derived from AAA-stacked buckled honeycomb layers. Magnetic measurements revealed that orthorhombic NLaCTO exhibits a long-range antiferromagnetic order below 13 K, as confirmed by DC and AC susceptibility and a λ-type heat-capacity anomaly, whereas hexagonal NYCTO exhibits glassy magnetic freezing below 11 K, characterized by frequency-dependent AC susceptibility and slow spin dynamics. Despite comparable Co2+-O-Co2+ exchange pathways and Co-topologies are retained in both structures, their contrasting magnetic behavior demonstrates that subtle structural differences can strongly reshape the magnetic energy landscape. These results establish chemical-unit substitution as an effective strategy for controlling magnetism in Co2+-based honeycomb oxides.

title: Clinical Significance of Cytokines in Pediatric Patients With Acquired Aplastic Anemia.
abstract: There remains limited evidence regarding serum cytokine variations in the progression of acquired aplastic anemia (aAA). Therefore, this retrospective study analyzed 12 serum cytokines in 52 pediatric patients with aAA and 56 healthy donors (HDs) to understand their role in aAA. Compared with HD, higher concentrations of interleukin-2 (IL-2), IL-5, IL-8, IL-10, and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) were observed in aAA. Furthermore, patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA) showed higher IL-6 than non-severe aplastic anemia (NSAA) population, and their IL-8 levels inversely correlated with neutrophil counts. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified IL-2, IL-8, and IL-10 as independent candidate biomarkers associated with aAA. A combined receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of these 3 cytokines demonstrated good discriminative performance in distinguishing aAA from HD, with an optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.891. Our observations suggest that aberrant serum cytokine levels are associated with aAA progression through mechanisms involving immune dysregulation.

title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

title: A Novel SERPINC1 Mutation in a Teenager With Antithrombin Deficiency Leading to Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Vein Thrombosis: Implications for Diagnosis and Management.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is uncommon in adolescents, and hereditary thrombophilia should be considered in unprovoked or progressive cases. We report a 16-year-old Chinese male with pulmonary embolism and extensive deep vein thrombosis that progressed despite anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin followed by unfractionated heparin. Antithrombin (AT) activity was persistently reduced (36%-49%; reference range, 80%-120%), and activated partial thromboplastin time remained subtherapeutic despite heparin dose escalation, suggesting functional heparin resistance. Switching to argatroban achieved clinical stabilization. Whole-exome sequencing identified a previously unreported heterozygous SERPINC1 variant (NM_000488.4: exon5: c.1153 G > T; p.Gly385Cys), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The patient's mother and sister carried the same variant and had reduced AT activity. The patient was subsequently transitioned to rivaroxaban and remained asymptomatic during follow-up. AT activity remained reduced at 1 and 2 years, while follow-up imaging showed a reduction in pulmonary arterial thrombotic burden but persistent lower-extremity venous thrombi. This case highlights the importance of evaluating AT deficiency in young patients with unprovoked or progressive VTE and the need for further evidence to establish the clinical significance of novel SERPINC1 variants.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients.

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl2-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

title: Mitochondrial LONP1: Linking structure and function to context‑dependent roles in disease (Review).
abstract: Mitochondrial proteostasis is essential for maintaining organellar integrity, metabolic adaptation and cellular survival under physiological and stress conditions. Among mitochondrial quality control mechanisms, Lon peptidase 1 (LONP1) is an ATP‑dependent AAA+ serine protease localized predominantly in the mitochondrial matrix and plays a central role in the recognition and degradation of damaged or misfolded proteins. Recent structural, molecular and multi‑omics studies have expanded our understanding of LONP1 beyond proteolysis, implicating it in protein quality control, mitochondrial DNA maintenance, metabolic regulation and responses to oxidative and cellular stress. Increasing evidence also indicates that LONP1 functions are highly dependent on cellular and disease context, with both loss and gain of LONP1 activity associated with distinct pathological outcomes. The present review integrated recent structural and functional advances to establish a structure‑function framework for understanding how LONP1 coordinates proteolytic and chaperone‑like activities and how these functions are shaped by cellular and disease context. The present review further examined its roles in metabolic, neurodegenerative, reproductive, cardiovascular and malignant diseases, with particular emphasis on the context‑dependent consequences of LONP1 dysregulation and its emerging therapeutic potential. Finally, the present review highlighted unresolved questions concerning substrate recognition and specificity, the relative contributions of protease and chaperone‑like functions, disease‑specific directionality and the safety and feasibility of therapeutic modulation. These challenges need to be addressed to establish the functional and translational boundaries of LONP1.

title: Microplastic Detection in the Ascending Aorta: An Exploratory Study Using Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS).
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant environmental pollutants that have been detected in various human tissues. This pilot biomonitoring study explored polymer mass in dissected versus non-dissected ascending aortic tissue. A total of 16 ascending aortic samples (8 acute type A aortic dissection [AD] and 8 acute type B dissection with arch involvement but a non-dissected ascending aorta [ND]) were examined using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) to screen 11 polymers. Both groups had aortic disease. Polymer-related signals were reported in all samples, with total mass estimates ranging from 1.92 to 155.58 µg/g tissue. The predominant reported polymer was polyamide 66 (PA66; 50.7%), followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC; 40.5%) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET; 8.8%). AD tissues showed a 3.9-fold higher estimated polymer burden than ND tissues (74.51 ± 42.81 vs. 19.25 ± 16.48 µg/g, p = 0.0077). PET estimates were also higher in AD tissues (7.36 ± 6.44 vs. 0.89 ± 1.49 µg/g, p = 0.025), but PET identification was tentative and polymer-specific tests were exploratory. Total polymer mass correlated with ascending aortic diameter (Spearman's rho = 0.865, p < 0.001). The age- and group-adjusted association (coefficient 0.079 mm per µg/g; p = 0.0098) was sensitive to omission of one observation (p = 0.140). These findings describe a difference in estimated polymer burden between two diseased-tissue groups. Incomplete analytical validation and possible perioperative contamination limit interpretation; particle identity, tissue localization, vascular toxicity and causality were not established. Further analytical and multicenter validation is needed.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

MAIN SYMPTOMS AND IMPORTANT CLINICAL FINDINGS: A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved.

MAIN DIAGNOSES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS, AND OUTCOMES: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

title: Fixed-Dose Combination Versus Add-On Therapy: Clarifying the Role of Cilostazol-Rosuvastatin in Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: The randomized trial by Kemalasari et al. provides evidence supporting the addition of cilostazol to rosuvastatin in patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease. However, because the study compared the fixed-dose combination (FDC) with rosuvastatin plus placebo, it does not establish whether the FDC formulation offers advantages over an equivalent free-combination regimen. Evidence from other cardiovascular settings suggests that FDC formulations may improve medication adherence and treatment persistence, although their effects on long-term clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Future randomized studies directly comparing fixed-dose and free-combination regimens, with adherence assessed over 12 months and longer-term cardiovascular and limb outcomes evaluated, are needed to clarify the clinical value of the formulation itself.

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

title: Global landscape and evolution of limb-salvage reconstruction with prostheses for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours: A bibliometric analysis.
abstract: PurposeTo delineate the evolution, collaborative structure, clinically relevant themes, and emerging priorities of limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from 1 January 1995 to 31 October 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on 31 October 2025. Co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses were conducted using CiteSpace 6.4.1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20.ResultsOf 2,606 retrieved records, 2,283 underwent title and abstract screening and 997 were included. Publication output increased, peaking at 84 in 2023. The United States led publication output and cumulative citations, while China ranked second by output. Keyword analyses indicated that research attention expanded from surgical strategy selection for specific tumour types and anatomical sites to include long-term prosthetic survival, complications and functional outcomes. Recent research themes included technologies such as 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and finite element analysis, with "3d printing" showing the strongest keyword burst (strength 9.49; 2021-2025). Research output was concentrated in a small number of centres and journals. Frequently co-cited publications provided standardised methods for assessing limb function and classifying endoprosthetic failure.ConclusionsLong-term prosthetic survival, complications, function and quality of life remain central themes in limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction. Technologies supporting individualised reconstruction, including 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and emerging robot-assisted techniques, are attracting increasing research interest. Future multicentre comparative studies should use standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up to evaluate prosthesis design, fixation and selection, as well as strategies for preventing and managing reconstructive failure.

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetic Foot Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Perfusion Assessment, and Implications for Pre-Revascularization Evaluation.
abstract: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of ulceration, infection, lower-extremity amputation, and premature mortality. Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes. Its implications for interpreting perfusion tests, assessing prognosis, and evaluating patients before revascularization remain insufficiently integrated in the existing literature. This narrative review examines MAC as a distal arterial phenotype with diagnostic and prognostic relevance in diabetic foot disease. Targeted PubMed searches updated on 22 September 2026, supplemented by reference checking and topic-specific searches, informed a qualitative synthesis of clinical, imaging, and mechanistic studies. The review distinguishes medial from intimal calcification and evaluates recognition, scoring, and renal, metabolic, and neurovascular mechanisms. Observational cohorts of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) and chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) link higher calcification burden with delayed healing, amputation, incomplete haemodynamic improvement, and selected systemic outcomes, although adjustment and endpoint definitions vary. In the MAC-prone diabetic foot, reliance on the ankle-brachial index alone may be misleading because calcified tibial and pedal arteries can produce falsely normal or elevated ankle pressures. Toe pressure, toe-brachial index (TBI), transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2), skin perfusion pressure (SPP), anatomical imaging, and careful wound trajectory assessment should therefore be integrated with established limb-threat and anatomical classifications. Emerging evidence suggests that MAC scoring may complement Wound, Ischaemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) staging, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) assessment, and small artery disease scoring in estimating wound-healing probability and amputation risk before revascularization. MAC scoring remains an adjunctive risk marker rather than a validated determinant of revascularization modality or a proven therapeutic target. Prospective studies should determine whether adding MAC assessment to established clinical models improves management and patient outcomes.

title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.

METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.

RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.

CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis. METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Sirtuins in cellular senescence and cardiovascular diseases: From mechanistic basis to activator development and translational perspectives.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated.

RESULTS: No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

title: Nursing-Related Risk Characteristics and Identification of High-Risk Patients With In-Hospital Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract:
AIM: Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024. Of 783 patients screened, 71 were excluded, leaving 712 in the source cohort (61 DVT cases and 651 ultrasound-negative, matchable controls). Cases and controls were matched 1:3 without replacement by age (±5 years), sex, and fracture site, yielding 61 matched sets (244 patients). After matching, non-matching variables were singly imputed using a random forest algorithm for the primary analysis. To assess uncertainty associated with this approach, a separate sensitivity analysis generated 20 completed datasets from the pre-imputation matched records using a stochastic chained-equation multiple-imputation procedure. Regression estimates across the 20 datasets were combined using Rubin's rules. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Incremental within-set concordance was corrected using 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples. The primary analysis, complete-case analyses and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis were conducted separately.

RESULTS: Matching variables were well balanced after matching, with standardized mean differences (SMD) of 0.02 for age and 0 for sex and fracture site, although several non-matching characteristics remained imbalanced. Three factors were positively associated with in-hospital DVT: admission Caprini ≥9 (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.28-4.61), severe POD1 activity dependence (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.38-10.94), and preoperative immobilization ≥72 h (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.14-5.67). Compared with patients without any core risk features, the OR increased to 2.81 (95% CI 1.46-5.38) among those with one feature and to 6.28 (95% CI 1.57-25.03) among those with two features. Adding severe POD1 activity dependence to Caprini ≥9 was associated with a modest increase in corrected within-set concordance from 0.589 to 0.633, corresponding to a difference of 0.044 (bootstrap SE 0.022, 95% CI 0.003-0.088). Sensitivity analyses generally preserved the direction of the main associations, although the Caprini estimate was attenuated after additional adjustment for trauma-related variables and D-dimer.

CONCLUSIONS: Admission Caprini ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h, and severe POD1 activity dependence were each associated with in-hospital lower-extremity DVT. POD1 activity assessment was associated with a modest improvement in within-set risk ranking beyond Caprini stratification. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; however, it may help guide nursing attention toward prophylaxis delivery, activity support, and symptom surveillance. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its clinical relevance.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024.

title: NLRP3+ Macrophages: Central Inflammatory Nodes of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm and Potential Cellular Target of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal inflammatory vascular disease without effective clinical treatments. Dietary patterns regulate aortic inflammation, and Mediterranean diet-derived omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFA) exert anti-inflammatory effects, yet their cellular targets in AAA remain unclear. We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells. Pseudo-bulk analysis and CoVarNet multicellular network analysis revealed a core remodeling axis: protective FOLR2+ resident macrophages were depleted, while a unique AAA-enriched NLRP3+ inflammatory macrophage population (M08_Mph_NLRP3) formed the hub of pathological inflammatory networks. Three bulk transcriptomic cohorts and five complementary enrichment approaches verified this signature. An LPS/OX-LDL/IL-1β-stimulated THP-1 model recapitulated AAA macrophage pathological changes including NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation, enhanced proliferation and migration. Further functional tests demonstrated ω-3 PUFA markedly blocked inflammasome cascade, reduced IL-1β/IL-18 release and reversed all macrophage pathological phenotypes. This study identifies M08_Mph_NLRP3 as the important inflammatory mediator of AAA and provides single-cell and in vitro functional evidence supporting ω-3 PUFA as a candidate nutritional agent targeting NLRP3-driven vascular inflammation.

We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells.

title: Early-onset Pulmonary Embolism After Prolonged Combined Cosmetic Breast Surgery: 2 Case Reports and a Literature Review.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures. Procedures lasted 225 and 370 minutes, respectively. Dyspnea, chest discomfort, or palpitations occurred within 48 hours postoperatively. D-dimer was elevated, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed acute PE, including a saddle embolus in 1 patient. Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin followed by rivaroxaban led to clinical improvement without observed recurrence at the short-term follow-up. A focused literature review identified additional thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast surgery, most within the first postoperative week. Early-onset PE can complicate prolonged, combined cosmetic breast surgery even in patients classified as intermediate risk. Pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis before symptom onset could not be reliably ascertained from available records. These cases support a protocolized, Caprini-informed pathway that specifies routine mechanical measures and clear indications, agent/dose, and timing for chemoprophylaxis, with explicit documentation and vigilance for early postoperative cardiopulmonary symptoms.

However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures.

title: Pantothenate metabolic alterations in PROS1 mutation carriers and the antithrombotic effects of pantethine.
abstract: Background Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1‑mutation patients through integrated multi‑omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models. Methods Serum metabolomics, siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed. Results Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM‑1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF‑κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL‑1β‑induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM‑1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine‑conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co‑incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation‑driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet mode of interaction. Conclusions This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet association in Protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1‑deficient in vivo models.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Endovascular Treatment for Ruptured Internal Carotid Artery Pseudoaneurysms Secondary to Radiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract:
AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of endovascular intervention in treating ruptured internal carotid artery (ICA) pseudoaneurysms secondary to radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed. Balloon test occlusion (BTO) was performed selectively when parent artery occlusion (PAO) was considered feasible. Treatment was individualized using covered stent implantation, coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, or PAO. Outcomes included final angiographic hemostasis, recurrent bleeding, complications (analyzed as events when patients had more than one event), and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at last follow-up.

RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were analyzed: 15 underwent coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, 12 covered stent implantation, and 5 PAO. BTO was performed in 8 patients (25.0%): 5 tolerated BTO and underwent PAO, whereas 3 had inadequate collateral reserve and received reconstructive treatment. Final angiographic hemostasis was achieved in all 32 patients (100%; 95% exact CI 89.1-100%). At last follow-up, 28 patients (87.5%; 95% CI 71.0%-96.5%) had mRS 0-1. Six complication events were recorded across 32 procedures (18.8 events per 100 procedures): 4 recurrent bleeding events and 2 transient limb weakness events, graded as Medical Research Council muscle-power grade 3. One patient contributed both recurrent bleeding and transient weakness; therefore event rates should not be interpreted as unique-patient incidence. No severe complications were observed.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular treatment achieved immediate hemostasis in this small, retrospective series of ruptured radiation-related ICA pseudoaneurysms. Treatment should be individualized according to collateral reserve, vascular anatomy, and the feasibility of BTO. Covered stents and coil-based reconstruction can preserve the parent artery but require close surveillance for endoleak, residual pseudoaneurysm, and new lesions. PAO may be considered only when collateral circulation is adequate; the zero-event estimate in five patients has a wide confidence interval. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed.

title: Development and application of evaluation criteria for venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies during the perioperative period.
abstract: BackgroundPatients with gynecologic malignancies face a high perioperative VTE risk and suboptimal prevention adherence, yet lack systematic, evidence-based evaluation standards.ObjectiveTo develop and preliminarily validate evidence-based, comprehensive evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in this population.MethodsThe Delphi method was employed to formulate the evaluation criteria for VTE prevention in this population. The Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) was used to assign a weight to each indicator, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was applied to evaluate adherence to perioperative VTE prevention standards among patients undergoing gynecologic surgery at our hospital.ResultsThe final criteria included 12 indicators covering quantitative and dynamic VTE risk assessment, bleeding risk evaluation, implementation of basic prophylaxis, assessment of indications and contraindications for mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis, timing, dosing, and duration of anticoagulant prophylaxis, and monitoring of efficacy and safety. The indicator weight coefficients ranged from 0.0234 to 0.1357. Among the 107 patients, 62 (57.94%) had Ci ≥ 0.6, and 45 (42.06%) had Ci < 0.6. Indicator-level analysis showed 100% compliance for basic prophylaxis, mechanical prophylaxis indications, and absence of contraindications to pharmacologic prophylaxis. The lowest compliance rates were observed for quantitative VTE risk assessment (25.23%, 27/107), dynamic VTE risk assessment (32.71%, 35/107), initiation timing (24.30%, 26/107), prophylaxis duration (24.30%, 26/107), and efficacy and safety monitoring (14.95%, 16/107).ConclusionThis study developed scientifically grounded and clinically feasible evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies. They provide a practical basis for quality improvement and ongoing refinement of institutional VTE prevention strategies.

title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
abstract: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.

Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers. In vitro, small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis.

title: Ischemic electrocardiographic changes and initial misdiagnosis of acute aortic syndromes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Ischemic electrocardiographic (ECG) changes can mimic acute myocardial infarction and obscure acute aortic dissection (AAD) or other acute aortic syndromes (AAS), but their association with initial misdiagnosis has not been synthesized. We assessed whether ischemic changes on the earliest prediagnostic ECG were associated with initial misdiagnosis.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure through July 1, 2026, for observational studies of confirmed AAD/AAS reporting 2 × 2 data for initial misdiagnosis by ischemic ECG status. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled with a random-effects model using restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity, QUIPS risk of bias, and GRADE certainty were assessed.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts from four countries included 724 cases; 609 had analyzable ECG data, including 179 initial misdiagnoses. Ischemic ECG changes were not significantly associated with initial misdiagnosis (pooled unadjusted OR, 1.419; 95% CI, 0.608-3.312; P = 0.351; 95% prediction interval, 0.223-9.039; I2 = 62.9%). All leave-one-out 95% CIs included 1.0. Excluding the principal contributor to heterogeneity yielded an OR of 1.050 (95% CI, 0.591-1.865) with negligible residual heterogeneity. No QUIPS domain was at high risk; GRADE certainty was moderate after downgrading for serious imprecision.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence did not demonstrate a significant association, but wide confidence and prediction intervals and unadjusted retrospective data leave important effects unresolved. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized ECG timing, harmonized diagnostic criteria, and multivariable adjustment are needed.

We assessed whether ischemic changes on the earliest prediagnostic ECG were associated with initial misdiagnosis. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure through July 1, 2026, for observational studies of confirmed AAD/AAS reporting 2 × 2 data for initial misdiagnosis by ischemic ECG status.

title: Case Report: Suspected Lower Limb Congestive Injury Associated with Decreased Compliance of the External Iliac Vein After Laparoscopic Myomectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of lower extremity deep vein thrombosis following gynecologic laparoscopy is 4.0%, whereas postoperative well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) is much rarer, with a reported incidence of only 0.03%-0.20%. Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 44-year-old woman underwent an 8-hour gynecologic laparoscopic procedure in the Lloyd-Davies position. Thirty minutes after surgery, she developed acute swelling, pain, and numbness of the right lower limb. Deep vein thrombosis was initially suspected, but treatment was ineffective. Unilateral well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) was subsequently considered, and her symptoms were relieved following supportive treatment, including dehydration therapy and elevation of the affected limb. Repeated review of the surgical video suggested lower limb congestive injury potentially associated with decreased compliance of the external iliac vein. The patient also experienced persistent postoperative symptoms resembling venous intermittent claudication, consistent with the clinical manifestations of impaired external iliac venous outflow.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the need for increased attention to the condition of the external iliac vascular sheath during gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Swelling and thickening of the vascular sheath, resulting in decreased compliance of the venous wall, may lead to severe venous congestion injury of the lower limb and may require timely intraoperative intervention when necessary. This case may provide a reference for the clinical diagnosis and management of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain following gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.

Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature.
