title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke.

title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA).

RESULTS: Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow.

CONCLUSIONS: Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD.

title: Combined antegrade-retrograde technique in urgent carotid stenting for true lumen compression after total arch replacement.
abstract: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow. Postprocedural imaging confirmed patency without major complications. This technique highlights a viable salvage strategy for managing complex aortic dissections when traditional methods fail. A literature review discusses the combined antegrade-retrograde approach used in urgent carotid stenting, as well as the advantages of ultrasound in selecting the true lumen and its minimally invasive nature.
englishSummary: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Rivaroxaban versus LMWH Thromboprophylaxis Following Gynecologic Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Comparison Study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban vs low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic cancer surgery.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to adjust for potential confounding factors.

RESULTS: A total of 250 women were included, 134 received rivaroxaban and 116 received LMWH for postoperative thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic malignancy-related surgery. After adjusting for potential confounding factors using multivariable logistic regression, the 30-day VTE and bleeding events showed no significant differences between the rivaroxaban group and the LMWH groups. There were no cases of 30-day readmission related to surgery, no 30-day mortality, and no all-cause mortality during the 1-year follow-up. Notably, all distal DVT events in both groups were calf muscular vein thromboses. During the 1-year follow-up, no patients were rehospitalized or died due to VTE.

CONCLUSION: We observed no significant differences in short- and long-term outcomes between rivaroxaban and LMWH after gynecologic malignancy surgery. Given the retrospective design and limited number of events, these results should be interpreted with caution, and prospective randomized studies are warranted.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban vs low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic cancer surgery. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h.

title: Pipeline embolization device with adjunctive coiling for ruptured blood blister-like aneurysms: a multicenter study focusing on Hunt-Hess grade I-III patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood blister-like aneurysms (BBAs) of the internal carotid artery are rare and inherently unstable lesions that carry a high risk of rebleeding. Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of PED combined with adjunctive coil embolization using a deliberate loose-scaffolding strategy.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. Immediate complete angiographic occlusion (modified Raymond-Roy class I) was observed in 67.9% (19/28), increasing to 75.0% (21/28) overall at 12 months and reaching 95.5% (21/22) among those with available imaging follow-up. Notably, all seven patients with residual neck filling on immediate postoperative angiography who completed follow-up subsequently achieved complete occlusion. Favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) was recorded in 92.9% (26/28) at last follow-up. Perioperative complications occurred in 39.3% (11/28), predominantly neurological, including symptomatic vasospasm (21.4%, 6/28) and cerebral infarction (14.3%, 4/28); perioperative mortality was 3.6% (1/28).

CONCLUSION: PED-assisted coil embolization with a loose-scaffolding strategy is technically feasible and may yield favorable outcomes in selected patients with mild-to-moderate neurologic deficits. However, given the retrospective, single-arm design and modest sample size, these results are hypothesis-generating; prospective comparative studies are warranted.

Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs.

title: "Inflammation-Thrombosis Dissociation": a retrospective study of early DVT differences after UKA between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3. Demographic characteristics, platelet count, hemoglobin, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were collected. Propensity score matching was used to control differences in age, sex, and body mass index, and Firth logistic regression was used to analyze factors associated with DVT.

RESULTS: Among the 147 patients, 14 developed postoperative DVT, for an overall incidence of 9.52%. The DVT incidence was 4.30% (4/93) in Tibetan patients, lower than the 18.52% (10/54) observed in Han Chinese patients (P = 0.007). Platelet count, D-dimer, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were all higher in Tibetan than in Han Chinese patients; however, these higher values did not correspond to a higher DVT incidence. After 1:1 matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 16 matched pairs were obtained; DVT incidences were 18.8% in Han Chinese patients and 0% in Tibetan patients. The difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.250), although the direction of the association was consistent with that before matching. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression showed that increasing age was associated with higher odds of DVT in Model 2 (OR = 1.110, 95% CI: 1.028-1.211, P = 0.007). In the primary model adjusted for age and BMI (Model 3), Tibetan ethnicity was associated with lower odds of DVT than Han Chinese ethnicity (OR = 0.206, 95% CI: 0.038-0.948, P = 0.042). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for sex (Model 4: OR = 0.243, 95% CI: 0.040-1.376, P = 0.109). In exploratory models separately incorporating postoperative platelet count, D-dimer, systemic immune-inflammation index, or aggregate index of systemic inflammation (Models 5-8), the association between ethnicity and DVT remained statistically significant (all P < 0.05), whereas none of these laboratory indices showed a statistically significant association with DVT (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among high-altitude UKA patients receiving a uniform aspirin prophylaxis regimen, Han Chinese patients had a higher incidence of early postoperative DVT than Tibetan patients. Although Tibetan patients had higher platelet counts and composite inflammatory indices, these measures did not increase in parallel with DVT events, suggesting a possible dissociation between inflammatory phenotype and clinical thrombotic risk among different ethnic groups at high altitude. Age and ethnicity were relatively stable DVT-associated factors in this cohort, whereas platelet count, D-dimer, and platelet-inflammation composite indices were insufficient to explain the between-ethnicity difference in risk. Given the single-center retrospective design and the limited number of outcome events and matched patients, these findings require further validation in multicenter, large-sample prospective studies.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3.

title: Modified Hybrid Repair with Open Reconstruction of Infrarenal Aortoiliac Segment for Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms Without Custom Distal Landing Zone: A Single-Center Case Series.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate distal landing zones can limit hybrid repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA). We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025. Open aneurysm excision and aortoiliac reconstruction provided the distal sealing segment and inflow for visceral and renal bypasses. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative length of hospital stay, 30-day major complication rate, 30-day paraplegia rate, 1-year reintervention rate, 30-day readmission rate, and technical success rate. Results: Five patients had Crawford extent II aneurysms and four had extent III aneurysms. Technical success was achieved in all nine patients. Median operative time, estimated blood loss, and intensive care unit stay were 724 min, 2500 mL, and 8 days, respectively. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 0% (0/9). No spinal cord ischemia or mesenteric ischemia occurred within 30 days. Acute kidney injury occurred in six patients (66.7%), including one who received continuous renal replacement therapy. One patient required early covered stent-graft repair of a right iliac anastomotic leak. At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6-12), all reconstructed visceral and renal bypasses were patent, no new endoleak was detected, and all patients were alive. No additional reintervention was required. Conclusions: Modified hybrid repair with prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction was technically feasible in selected TAAA patients with inadequate distal sealing anatomy. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to evaluate durability and refine indications.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance.

METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set.

RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set.

CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool.

RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Association of muscle strength with the incidence of venous thromboembolism and all-cause mortality among patients: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Muscle strength is a well-established indicator of overall health, yet its prospective association with the incidence and prognosis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains inconsistent.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident VTE and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.72 years, 15 774 incident VTE events were documented. Each 1-standard deviation increase in muscle strength was associated with a 13% reduction in VTE risk (HR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). Compared with the low muscle strength group, participants in the middle and high tertiles had 12% (HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.92) and 19% (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.77-0.84) lower risk of VTE. This inverse association remained consistent across all genetic risk strata. Among patients with VTE, 2884 deaths occurred during follow-up. Each 1-standard deviation increase was associated with a 14% lower mortality risk (HR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.82-0.90). High and middle muscle strength were associated with 21% (HR 0.79, 95% CI: 0.72-0.87) and 17% (HR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.76-0.91) lower all-cause mortality versus low strength.

CONCLUSION: Higher muscle strength is associated with a lower risk of incident VTE, regardless of genetic predisposition, and with lower mortality among patients with VTE.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles.

title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088).

CONCLUSION: A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes.

title: Catheter-related deep vein thrombosis complicated by iatrogenic pulmonary embolism after thrombectomy leading to hemodialysis failure and successful rescue by automated peritoneal dialysis: A case report.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Catheter-related deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a serious complication in hemodialysis (HD) patients and may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE). Interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT may be complicated by acute PE and other life-threatening events. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance make HD unsustainable, automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) may provide an alternative renal replacement strategy. We report a case of successful rescue with APD after severe complications following interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT.

PATIENT CONCERNS: An 82-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease developed right femoral vein thrombosis shortly after initiating urgent-start HD via a femoral catheter. Following percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis, she developed acute hypoxemia, pulmonary embolism, severe thrombocytopenia, heart failure, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Recurrent central venous catheter dysfunction and repeated hypotension and oxygen desaturation during HD made continued conventional HD increasingly difficult.

DIAGNOSES: The patient was diagnosed with catheter-related DVT complicated by acute PE following interventional thrombectomy.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received intensive supportive care, including anticoagulation when clinically feasible, continuous renal replacement therapy, blood transfusions, and management of gastrointestinal bleeding and heart failure. Because of recurrent central venous catheter dysfunction and intolerance to conventional HD, a multidisciplinary team recommended peritoneal dialysis (PD). After clinical stabilization and PD catheter placement, she was transitioned to APD.

OUTCOMES: After APD initiation, the patient's uremic symptoms and lower-extremity edema resolved, and her functional capacity improved from bedridden to independent walking. Hemoglobin increased from 65.7 to 118.2 g/L, cardiac function improved, and adequate dialysis was achieved with a total dialysis adequacy index of 2.58. During approximately 10 months of follow-up, she remained free from peritonitis and PD catheter dysfunction.

LESSONS: This case highlights the risk of serious thromboembolic complications following interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT in HD patients. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance render conventional HD unsustainable, timely reassessment of dialysis modality is crucial; APD may offer an effective rescue strategy for selected elderly patients.

Interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT may be complicated by acute PE and other life-threatening events. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance make HD unsustainable, automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) may provide an alternative renal replacement strategy.

title: Development and internal validation of machine-learning models for postoperative deep vein thrombosis after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture: evaluation of Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome features.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains a clinically important complication after hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. We evaluated whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome features add predictive information beyond conventional preoperative variables and examined the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and postoperative DVT.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 380 patients. Group-constrained partitioning and resampling prevented identical prespecified multivariable profiles from crossing evaluation boundaries, yielding a development set (n = 267; 74 DVT events) and a profile-disjoint held-out validation set (n = 113; 31 events). Nine machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using a fixed eight-variable panel comprising D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet count, type 2 diabetes, fasting blood glucose, TyG, Qi stagnation with blood stasis (QSBS), and Qi deficiency with blood stasis (QDBS). Random forest (RF) was selected on the basis of development-set out-of-fold performance before held-out validation.

RESULTS: Postoperative DVT occurred in 105 patients (27.6%). RF achieved a pooled group-aware development out-of-fold AUC of 0.774 (95% CI 0.710-0.837) and a held-out validation AUC of 0.859 (95% CI 0.782-0.935). Across 30 repeated group-constrained partitions, mean validation AUC was 0.792. In the single profile-disjoint held-out validation partition, the development-derived threshold of 0.298 yielded sensitivity of 0.903, specificity of 0.720, positive predictive value of 0.549, and negative predictive value of 0.952; in that same partition, the calibration slope was 1.136 (95% CI 0.753-1.867), the observed-to-expected ratio was 0.846, and the Brier score was 0.132. Adding QSBS and QDBS did not materially improve discrimination (AUC 0.855 vs. 0.859; ΔAUC = 0.003; DeLong p = 0.746). Higher TyG remained associated with DVT after multivariable adjustment (OR per 1 SD 1.550, 95% CI 1.186-2.026; p = 0.001); restricted cubic splines supported an overall association (p = 0.007) without significant evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.082).

CONCLUSION: RF showed favorable discrimination in the held-out cohort but more modest performance across repeated group-constrained partitions. The two retained TCM syndrome variables did not provide a material increment in AUC, whereas higher TyG remained associated with postoperative DVT after multivariable adjustment. External validation and assessment of recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

We evaluated whether Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome features add predictive information beyond conventional preoperative variables and examined the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and postoperative DVT. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 380 patients.

title: Serial computed tomography angiography-based computational fluid dynamics characterizes reduced near-renal tear exchange in kidneys that develop atrophy after aortic dissection repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal atrophy may develop after aortic dissection repair despite an anatomically patent renal artery on computed tomography angiography (CTA). This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss.

METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models were built from preoperative, early postoperative and late follow-up CTA; within each patient, inlet and outlet (three-element Windkessel) boundary conditions were identical across time points. All 90 true-lumen/false-lumen (TL/FL) communications were characterized by distance from the renal-ostial plane, direction, pressure difference and trans-tear flow. TL/FL relationships were quantified at the renal-ostial plane, and bilateral renal-artery flow was computed directly. Renal volume was measured by three-dimensional CTA segmentation.

RESULTS: All six index kidneys were supplied from the FL before repair. Index-kidney volume changed by -53.0%, -64.1% and -50.6% in the atrophy group and by -13.8%, +0.8% and -10.7% in comparators. No hemodynamic measure separated the groups before repair. From the early postoperative model onward (3-37 days), two aortic-level flow measures were lower in every atrophy kidney than in every comparator: the FL flow-magnitude fraction at the renal-ostial plane (0.03-0.10 versus 0.13-0.79) and total peak-systolic trans-communication flow (37.8-45.1 versus 61.8-185.3 mL/s). Index renal-artery flow separated the groups only at late follow-up (-29.4%, -32.6% and -63.9% versus +5.9%, -7.4% and -3.0%), as did tear-exchange flow directed toward the renal-ostial level (1.9-19.1 versus 38.7-130.9 mL/s). FL/TL pressure ratios did not separate the groups at any time point. In one patient-derived geometry, sequential virtual closure of idealized communications redistributed and reversed flow in the remaining communications; index renal-artery flow after the final closure was similar to baseline.

CONCLUSION: In kidneys that later atrophied, the FL flow contribution at the renal level was lower than in comparators early after repair, before the modeled decrease in renal-artery flow and, in two of three kidneys, before substantial volume loss. Given three kidneys per group and multiple measures, these associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causation, renal parenchymal perfusion or a treatment threshold.

This exploratory study compared serial near-renal aortic hemodynamics between kidneys with and without later renal-volume loss. METHODS: Six index kidneys from six men were studied: three with ≥30% loss of reference volume (atrophy group) and three age-matched comparators.

title: Prognostic performance of the WIfI classification in diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI after endovascular revascularization: a subgroup analysis of the PRIME-WIFI registry.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification is widely used in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population.

METHODS: This subgroup analysis of the prospective, multicenter PRIME-WIFI registry included diabetic patients with infrapopliteal CLTI undergoing endovascular revascularization. Associations between baseline WIfI stage and MAE (all-cause mortality, major amputation, or clinically driven target-limb reintervention), its individual components, amputation-free survival, clinical improvement, and 12-month VascuQoL change were assessed using Kaplan-Meier, multivariable Cox, and Harrell's C-index analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 707 diabetic patients (730 limbs) were analyzed; in the full PRIME-WIFI cohort, diabetes status showed a borderline interaction with WIfI stage for MAE (P for interaction = 0.083). One-year freedom from MAE decreased across WIfI stages (89.5%, 77.4%, 78.0%, and 70.1% for stages 1-4; log-rank P = 0.004), and WIfI stage independently predicted MAE (HR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.09-1.56; P = 0.0031). One-year AFS was 94.7%, 83.3%, 83.3%, and 74.2% (log-rank P = 0.0003), with higher WIfI stage associated with worse AFS (HR: 1.53; 95% CI: 1.24-1.89; P < 0.001). Overall survival was 94.7%, 87.8%, 86.1%, and 80.3% (log-rank P = 0.009), and WIfI stage was independently associated with mortality (HR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.20-1.94; P < 0.001). Freedom from major amputation was 100.0%, 95.3%, 96.8%, and 92.3% (log-rank P = 0.02), with higher WIfI stage independently associated with major amputation (HR: 1.62; 95% CI: 1.07-2.57; P = 0.020). In contrast, freedom from CD-TLR did not differ significantly across stages (log-rank P = 0.60; HR: 0.92; 95% CI: 0.68-1.23; P = 0.564). Clinical improvement tended to decrease with increasing WIfI stage but did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.053). VascuQoL scores improved from baseline to 12 months across all WIfI stages, with no significant difference in the magnitude of improvement among stages (time-by-WIfI interaction P = 0.247).

CONCLUSIONS: In this diabetic subgroup, WIfI retained prognostic value for MAE, AFS, mortality, and major amputation. However, discrimination was clearest between stages 1 and 4, with limited separation between stages 2 and 3. These findings support WIfI for broad risk stratification while highlighting the need for complementary assessment in diabetic CLTI.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification is widely used in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, its prognostic performance in diabetic patients after endovascular revascularization remains unclear. We evaluated its prognostic and discriminatory performance in this population.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared.

RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

title: The role of vascular factors in Alzheimer's disease: from cerebrovascular pathological mechanisms to blood biomarkers.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common dementia, and post-mortem and imaging studies consistently demonstrate that vascular pathology coexists with plaques and tangles in most AD brains. Vascular risk factors-hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, and atrial fibrillation-damage the neurovascular unit, disrupt the blood-brain barrier, and induce chronic hypoperfusion, thereby promoting β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, and neuroinflammation. Cerebral small vessel disease, amyloid angiopathy, and carotid stenosis are overrepresented in AD and accelerate cognitive decline. Ultrasensitive blood assays now enable plasma Aβ42/40, phosphorylated tau isoforms, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and neurofilament light chain to approach the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid and PET, while endothelial injury markers such as vascular endothelial-cadherin and soluble adhesion molecules are emerging. Against this background, this review contends that AD diagnostics must move beyond a single-pathology framework toward an integrated model that combines neurodegenerative and vascular injury biomarkers. Reliance on Aβ and tau alone cannot capture clinical heterogeneity nor guide vascular-targeted interventions. A multidimensional blood panel reflecting pericyte loss, endothelial dysfunction, and blood-brain barrier compromise may offer improved stratification and ultimately help identify whether a biomarker-defined subgroup could benefit from vascular interventions-a hypothesis that remains to be tested prospectively. This review traverses the entire cascade from risk factors through cerebrovascular mechanisms to surgical considerations and blood biomarkers, aiming to provide a clinically actionable reference for multidisciplinary dementia care.

title: Development of a multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for venous thromboembolism prevention in hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer: a mixed-methods modified Delphi study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common and potentially preventable complication in patients with lung cancer. Although clinical guidelines recommend risk assessment and appropriate prophylaxis, hospitals often lack operational frameworks for translating these recommendations into multidisciplinary workflows, quality monitoring, and continuous improvement. This study aimed to develop a hospital-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for VTE prevention and management among hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer.

METHODS: A mixed-methods modified Delphi study was conducted. Candidate framework items were generated from a structured literature review and semi-structured interviews with physicians, nurses, clinical pharmacists, and hospital managers, and were organized using Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 15 experts from respiratory medicine, oncology, clinical pharmacy, nursing management, and hospital quality management. Experts rated the importance and feasibility of each candidate item, and the framework was refined using predefined consensus criteria and qualitative feedback.

RESULTS: The response rate was 100% in both Delphi rounds. Expert authority coefficients were 0.943 and 0.953 in rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall's W ranged from 0.249 to 0.292, indicating low-to-moderate concordance despite statistically significant tests. The final framework included 3 first-level domains, 11 second-level components, and 34 third-level indicators covering structural capacity, care processes, and outcome monitoring. Importance ratings were generally higher than feasibility ratings, particularly for indicators requiring information system support, multidisciplinary coordination, and post-discharge continuity of care.

CONCLUSION: This study developed a preliminary, consensus-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for hospital-based VTE prevention in patients with lung cancer. The framework may support the operationalization of guideline recommendations, standardization of care processes, and prioritization of quality improvement efforts. Prospective implementation studies are needed to evaluate its feasibility, transferability, and impact on care quality and patient outcomes.

title: Emergent or urgent hybrid repair for complex thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms: single-centre experience.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Emergent or urgent repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) always represent a major challenge due to high mortality and complex reconstruction of visceral arteries. We aimed to evaluate the short- and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing emergent or urgent hybrid TAAA repair under a standardized institutional perioperative protocol.

METHODS: This study represents a retrospective cohort analysis of data derived from a prospectively maintained institutional database at West China Hospital. All consecutive patients who underwent emergent or urgent hybrid repair for TAAA between January 2013 and February 2025 were included.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 38 TAAA patients (31 male, with a median age of 50.5 years) who underwent emergent/urgent hybrid repair. The median aneurysm length was 200.9 mm (IQR 154.0-320.0), with a mean maximum diameter was 70.5 ± 17.8 mm. Intraoperatively, 4 visceral arteries (IQR 4-5) were reconstructed. Median operative time was 415 min (IQR 360-504), with median ICU and postoperative hospital stays of 96.0 h (IQR 46.5-203.5) and 17 days (IQR 11-24), respectively. No myocardial infarction or hepatic failure occurred. Postoperative complications included pulmonary infection (n = 4, 10.5%), acute kidney injury (n = 2, 5.3%), and spinal cord ischemia (n = 5, 13.2%). Thirty-day mortality was 10.5% (n = 4). The survival rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 86.8% (95% CI 76.7-98.3) and 83.0% (95% CI 71.7-96.6). The free of reintervention rates at 12 and 60 months postoperatively were 90.5% (95% CI 80.8-100.0) and 76.4% (95% CI 61.1-95.7).

CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort managed with a standardized perioperative protocol, emergent and urgent hybrid TAAA repair was feasible, with acceptable perioperative mortality and durable mid- to long-term survival. However, the occurrence of spinal cord ischemia represents a substantial and clinically significant trade-off of this approach in the emergency setting. Moreover, these favorable survival outcomes should be interpreted in the context of the cohort's relatively young age and favorable baseline risk profile. These findings emphasize that survival benefit is counterbalanced by significant neurological morbidity, highlighting the need for refined spinal protection protocols in urgent cases and for comparative studies to validate the specific efficacy of this standardized protocol.

We aimed to evaluate the short- and long-term outcomes of patients undergoing emergent or urgent hybrid TAAA repair under a standardized institutional perioperative protocol. METHODS: This study represents a retrospective cohort analysis of data derived from a prospectively maintained institutional database at West China Hospital.

title: Multimodal integration of carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics and dynamic systemic immune-inflammation trajectories for subacute risk stratification after stroke thrombectomy: development and internal validation of an exploratory prognostic model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We hypothesized that integrating macroscopic carotid plaque architecture, quantified via ultrasound radiomics, with downstream micro-cellular temporal dynamics, defined by longitudinal immune trajectories, would yield a highly accurate prognostic framework for 90-day functional outcomes in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery (N = 221) and an internal validation cohort (N = 95) using stratified random sampling. To capture temporal inflammatory heterogeneity, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) was measured at days 0, 1, 3, and 7, and clustered using Latent Class Mixed Models (LCMM). Concurrently, high-dimensional radiomic features strictly adhering to the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) guidelines were extracted from baseline two-dimensional carotid ultrasound images. A radiomics score (Rad-score) was constructed utilizing Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Four progressive predictive models were developed, culminating in an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) multimodal architecture. The primary endpoint was an unfavorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3 to 6).

RESULTS: An unfavorable outcome occurred in 166 of 316 patients (52.5%). The LCMM objectively identified three longitudinal SII phenotypes. The "persistent high-inflammation" trajectory (Class 3, 17.0% of patients) was independently associated with an increased risk of an unfavorable outcome compared to the "rapid resolution" trajectory (Class 1) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 4.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20 to 10.85; p < 0.001]. The ultrasound Rad-score, comprising 9 core textural features, also demonstrated robust independent predictive value (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92 per 0.1-point increase; p < 0.001). In the strictly isolated internal validation cohort, the full multimodal XGBoost model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86 to 0.97), with an accuracy of 86.3%, sensitivity of 88.0%, and specificity of 84.4%. This performance was statistically superior to the standard clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.84; p < 0.001 via DeLong test). Furthermore, the multimodal paradigm demonstrated clinical reclassification utility, yielding a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.985 (95% CI, 0.684 to 1.286) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (95% CI, 0.128 to 0.260).

CONCLUSION: An exploratory model integrating baseline carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics with Day-0-to-Day-7 systemic immune-inflammation trajectories was associated with 90-day functional outcome after EVT and, on internal validation, discriminated outcomes more strongly than a conventional clinical model. Because the immune-trajectory component is only complete at Day 7, the model is intended for subacute post-EVT risk stratification rather than acute treatment selection, and requires external, prospective validation before any clinical application.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery (N = 221) and an internal validation cohort (N = 95) using stratified random sampling.

title: Inflammation-associated clinical prognostic factors and primary patency after drug-coated balloon angioplasty for recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula stenosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis occurs in a vascular environment in which injury, neointimal hyperplasia and inflammation may coexist. Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. This retrospective study examines clinical outcomes and inflammation-related prognostic associations without assuming that inflammatory pathways were measured or causally established.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort comprised 357 patients treated between February 2023 and May 2026. The primary outcome was time from index DCB angioplasty to clinically driven target-lesion reintervention. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses used available follow-up; a separate clinical logistic model addressed failure within 12 months in 356 patients with complete model data. No non-DCB comparator or patient-level molecular measurements were available.

RESULTS: Mean brachial-artery flow increased from 288.98 ± 139.37 to 980.92 ± 174.66 mL/min and minimal luminal diameter from 1.52 ± 0.50 to 5.21 ± 0.63 mm (both P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier primary patency was 95.24%, 84.03%, 68.90%, and 55.40% at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. In the extended Cox model (338 patients; 191 events), previous PTA count (HR 1.129 per procedure, P = 0.003) and lesion length (HR 1.105 per cm, P = 0.001) were associated with greater hazard; postprocedural flow (HR 0.889 per 100 mL/min, P = 0.014) and red-blood-cell count (HR 0.804 per 1012/L, P = 0.027) were associated with lower hazard. The five-fold cross-validated AUC of the clinical 12-month model was 0.706.

CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center cohort, recurrent AVF stenosis after DCB angioplasty was associated with previous PTA burden, lesion length, postprocedural flow, and red-blood-cell count. Routine blood-cell measures provide an exploratory inflammation-related clinical context but do not establish inflammatory mechanisms or validate a specific inflammatory biomarker. Independent validation and patient-level inflammatory measurements are required.

Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. title: An asymptomatic pulmonary arteriovenous fistula presenting with a Campylobacter rectus brain abscess as the initial manifestation: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain abscess is a severe infectious disease of the central nervous system associated with high rates of mortality and morbidity. Pulmonary arteriovenous fistula (PAVF) is a rare but important cause of cryptogenic brain abscesses. The pathogens associated with PAVF-related brain abscesses are typically oral anaerobes or facultative anaerobes, most commonly non-hemolytic streptococci and Streptococcus intermedius. To our knowledge, no case of a monomicrobial Campylobacter rectus (C. rectus) brain abscess in a patient with asymptomatic PAVF has been reported.

CASE PRESENTATION: Herein, we report the case of a 57-year-old man with a C. rectus brain abscess in association with an asymptomatic PAVF. The patient presented to our hospital with fever and headache. Magnetic resonance (MR) imaging revealed a 5 × 2 cm brain abscess in the right temporal and occipital lobes, surrounded by extensive edema. Enhanced computed tomography (CT) scanning of the lungs revealed both nodules and PAVF. Blood culture and cardiac ultrasound failed to detect any abnormalities. Piperacillin-tazobactam and meropenem were administered for anti-infection, although the headache persisted. He was subsequently transferred to neurosurgery to resect the abscess by craniotomy; postoperative pus culture confirmed the presence of C. rectus.

CONCLUSIONS: For brain abscesses caused by oral anaerobes such as C. rectus, screening for right-to-left shunting diseases such as PAVF may be considered when no other source is identified.

title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator.

RESULTS: Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73, p = 0.001; Gray's test p < 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98, p = 0.17; Gray's test p = 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68, p = 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86, p = 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not.

CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023.
